package.title: Tirzepatide: Why Hunger Returns After Stopping #shorts
package.description:
Hunger coming back after stopping tirzepatide isn't weakness — it's biology. In SURMOUNT-4 (adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, without diabetes; 335 stayed on their maximum tolerated dose, 335 switched to placebo), weight rose an average of 14.0% on placebo from week 36 to 88 and fell another 5.5% on tirzepatide (JAMA, online 11 Dec 2023). Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea and constipation.

Don't stop or change your medicine on your own — plan any change with your prescriber. Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2812936
https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/217806s000lbl.pdf

social.instagram_caption:
Hunger came back after stopping tirzepatide? That's not a willpower failure.

Here's the actual number: in the SURMOUNT-4 trial, adults with obesity (or overweight with a weight-related condition, no diabetes) took tirzepatide at their max tolerated dose for 36 weeks. Then 335 stayed on it and 335 switched to placebo.

From week 36 to week 88:
• Placebo group: weight rose an average of 14.0%
• Stayed on tirzepatide: lost another 5.5%

Why? Tirzepatide helps turn down appetite while you're taking it. When it stops, that effect fades, so hunger (and weight) tends to return. That's biology, not a character flaw.

Worth noting: even the placebo group was still averaging 9.9% below their starting weight at week 88.

Save this for the next time someone asks "what happens if I stop?"

Common side effects of tirzepatide include nausea, diarrhea and constipation. Don't stop or change your medicine on your own — plan any change with your prescriber.

#Tirzepatide #SURMOUNT4 #GLP1 #WeightManagement #ObesityScience #MetabolicHealth

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

If you've ever worried that hunger coming back after stopping tirzepatide means you did something wrong — it doesn't. There's real biology behind it.

In the SURMOUNT-4 trial, adults with obesity (or overweight plus a weight-related condition, no diabetes) took tirzepatide at their maximum tolerated dose for 36 weeks, then were split: 335 stayed on it, 335 switched to placebo. Tirzepatide helps quiet appetite while you're on it, and that effect fades once you stop — which is why weight tends to drift back. Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea and constipation, and any change to your treatment should be planned with your prescriber, not done on your own.

factcheck.summary: PASS. All the SURMOUNT-4 facts check out against the JAMA paper (Aronne et al., published online 11 Dec 2023, print JAMA 2024;331(1):38–48). That covers the population (adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, without diabetes), the 36-week lead-in at maximum tolerated dose (10 or 15 mg), 335 per arm, weeks 36–88 (placebo +14.0%, tirzepatide −5.5%), the treatment-regimen estimand, and placebo at −9.9% from the start at week 88. The safety lines are all there: don't stop or change on your own, the prescriber line, Not personal advice and common side effects. The CTA correctly falls back to "follow for more" without naming an unconfirmed video. The Zepbound label URL opens a real FDA PDF, but I couldn't extract its text, so I checked the side-effect list from memory. Three minor fixes: (1) s5's appetite explanation comes from the label's mechanism, not from SURMOUNT-4, which didn't measure appetite or hunger. Take src1 off s5 and soften the wording a little. (2) s4's on-screen text leaves out the timeframe. (3) s3's on-screen text doesn't name the two groups.
